# pluginlet

> **Status: experimental, source-only for now.** The package is not on npm yet; it installs from
> t

his repository's git URL. The release tooling (`scripts/release.mjs`, `RELEASING.md`) is in
> place
but has deliberately not been run against a registry — see "Releasing" when that changes.
Each `*.pluginlet` file in the workspace becomes **its own Conversation View tab**, so the tabs read

`对话 / 轨迹 / hello`. The repository carries its own pluginlets; whoever checks the
repository out get
s them, with no npm publish and no profile install per project.

Settings are not part of the plugin UI: they live in the harness's plugin configuration
(**Plugins →
Pluginlet**, or the `config:` block of this bundle's row).
| key | default | meaning |
| `devMode` | `false` | accept a changed hash without re-approval (still audited; writes/network/rea

ds still capped) |
| `extensions` | `['.pluginlet']` | which file names count as pluginlets |
| `dir

ectories` | `['.dsh/pluginlets']` | where to look, relative to the workspace root |
| `maxEditors` |

`64` | discovery cap |
| `maxEditorBytes` | `524288` | per-pluginlet source cap |
| `allowRead` / `

allowNetwork` / `allowWrite` | `true` | whether those capabilities may be offered at all |
| `net` |
`{ perMinute: 20, perHour: 240, maxBytes: 1048576 }` | network budget per pluginlet |
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Only `.dsh/pluginlets/` is scanned: a stray `*.pluginlet` at the repository root is not a tab.
Add m
ore directories with the `directories` setting if you need them.
## The authoring guide ships with the plugin
Applying the Host half registers one skill, `pluginlet-development`. Once the plugin is installed, a

ny
agent in the profile can load it before writing a pluginlet: it covers the three export shapes, t

he
`api` surface, every construct the scanner blocks, and the path rules that decide whether the
app
roval dialog asks for one file or the whole workspace.
The body lives in `skills/pluginlet-development.md`; `node test/skill.mjs` fails if a scanner rule o

r
a grantable capability is added without the skill documenting it.
## The pluginlet contract
A `.pluginlet` file is plain JavaScript — **no JSX, no imports** (the plugin is installed without a
build step, so there is no compiler in the loop). It exports one of three shapes:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`api` is the whole surface:
| member | meaning |

| `h`, `Fragment` | create elements |
| `useState`, `useEffect`, `useMemo`, `useRef`, `useCallback`

| hooks |
| `fs.read(path)`, `fs.list(path)` | **wrapped** filesystem reads, workspace-contained (ca

pability `fs:read`) |
| `net.fetch(url, init)` | **wrapped** network (capability `net:fetch`), rate-

limited and audited |
| `write.request(target, text, version)` | asks the user; **never writes by it

self** (capability `write:request`) |
| `ui.toast(message)` | transient message in the host |
| `met
a.name`, `meta.path` | this pluginlet's identity |
## Security model
The scanner is a policy gate, not the boundary. The boundary is the sandbox:

- the pluginlet runs in an iframe with `sandbox="allow-scripts"` (opaque origin: no access to the
ap

p's DOM, storage, or cookies) and a document CSP of `default-src 'none'` (no network, no
subresource

s, no fonts, no forms);
- therefore `fs` and `net` exist **only** as `postMessage` calls to the host

, which forwards them
to `/api/pluginlet/*`; every call is budgeted on both sides and written to the

audit log;
- a write is impossible without a click in the host's confirmation dialog: the frame's `

e `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `WebSocket`,
`process`, `localStorage`, `postMessage`, `navigator` are

**blocked by the scan and can never be
granted**. `document`/`window` are allowed on purpose: inside

the frame they are the frame's own
document, which the imperative `mount(el, api)` form needs, and

anonically after** (`ctx.fs.contains` on resolved
targets), so a symlink inside the workspace cannot

point a read or a listing outside it;
- the network proxy validates the hostname **and every addres

s it resolves to**, then follows
redirects by hand so each hop is validated again. A DNS answer that

changes between the check and
the connection (rebinding) is still possible; the proxy is a guard ra

il, not an egress filter;
- the approval dialog lists each capability with its **path scopes as chec

kboxes**: you can approve
a subset, and the pluginlet renders against exactly what it got (`api.acce

ss.can`);
- a running pluginlet can ask for more with `api.access.request(capability, scopes)` — one

he **content hash and a path scope**: a pluginlet that only touches `docs/readme.md`
is approved for

exactly that file, not for the repository. Scopes come from the source itself —
[该节后续省略]
## Host routes

All routes are `POST` under `/api/pluginlet/` and require `x-dsh-plugin: pluginlet`
(a cross-site pa
ge cannot send a custom header without a preflight this server never answers).
| route | purpose |

| `discover` | list `*.pluginlet` at the root and in `.dsh/pluginlets/`, with content hashes |
| `sc

an` | static scan: blocked constructs, declared capabilities, notes |
| `source` | serve the source

**only** to an authorized hash (records the issued hash) |
| `state` / `grant` / `revoke` / `log` |

grants (`capability -> path scopes`), revocation, audit tail |
| `fs/list`, `fs/read` | wrapped read

s; the target must sit inside the granted scope, else `OUT_OF_SCOPE` |
| `net/fetch` | wrapped netwo

rk: http(s) only, no private hosts, 10s timeout, 1 MiB cap, 20/min + 240/h per pluginlet |
| `write`
| user-confirmed write, scope-checked, version-guarded (`409 STALE`), explicit `workspace-write` po
r-confirmed write, scope-checked, version-guarded (`409 STALE`), explicit `workspace-write` policy |

Every path is resolved inside a registered workspace root; reads go through `ctx.fs`, never raw
`nod

path is resolved inside a registered workspace root; reads go through `ctx.fs`, never raw
`node:fs`.
